summary: Uru Harbour Airport (ATD/AGAT) is a small regional airport serving the community of Atoifi in Malaita Province, Solomon Islands. Situated near the northern coast of Malaita Island, it provides essential air connectivity for residents and visitors traveling to this remote part of the country. The airport operates as a key link for local transportation, supporting small aircraft that connect to Honiara and other Solomon Islands destinations.
faqs:
Q: What types of aircraft serve Uru Harbour Airport?
A: The airport primarily handles small turboprop aircraft operated by domestic carriers serving the Solomon Islands' regional routes.

Q: Are there scheduled commercial flights to this airport?
A: Limited scheduled domestic flights operate to Uru Harbour, typically connecting with Honiara on the main island of Guadalcanal.

Q: What facilities are available at the airport?
A: As a small rural airport, facilities are minimal, typically including a basic terminal building and limited passenger amenities.

Q: When is the best time to fly to this region?
A: The dry season months from May to October generally offer the most reliable flying conditions in the Solomon Islands.
transport_tips: Ground transportation options at Uru Harbour Airport are limited; travelers should arrange local pickup in advance as taxis and rental services are not commonly available on-site. Reaching Atoifi town from the airport typically requires a short road transfer along local routes. Visitors are advised to confirm onward transport arrangements before arrival, as mobile network coverage in the area can be inconsistent.
local_tip: Carry small denominations of Solomon Islands dollars (SBD) for any local purchases or informal transport arrangements, as card payment facilities are virtually nonexistent in the Atoifi area.
